about: Which of the certificates control hands out an account trusts now, from the root device a daemon pinned: each must chain back to that root (self-signed, of a kind that roots), every link signed by a device valid when the link was made, of a kind that certifies the next. A certificate not signed by the key of the device it names as approver is set aside before anything else. A recovery code lets in one device: the first it signed, by created time, then by device id. A revocation counts when its signer is valid then (checked twice, so a revoked device's own revocations stop counting); a browser or a recovery code is taken off only by a device that's a browser all the way to the root, along certificates that count (each a browser's, or a recovery code's above one). A device revoked at T no longer counts, nor what it approved after T; what it approved before T stays. Certificates don't expire: time matters only against revocations. Anything that doesn't check out is ignored, never an error: control may send junk, and it can only shrink the set.

input: account and root: what's pinned (the account, its root device's id); certs and revocations: labels of objects, in the order control sent them
output: trusted: the devices trusted now, sorted by id: each one's device id, name and approver (which of its certificates counted)
